title: Search a binary search tree for node 7
summary: Search for 7 among values 1 through 15, comparing at each node and choosing the left or right branch.
context: At any node in a binary search tree all values on the left are smaller and all on the right are larger than its value. Arrows lead from parent to child.

This perfect binary search tree has four levels with values 1 through 15. Root 8 has children 4 and 12, in left-to-right order. The children of 4 are 2 and 6, and of 12 are 10 and 14. The children of 2 are 1 and 3; of 6, 5 and 7; of 10, 9 and 11; and of 14, 13 and 15.
The pointer cur marks the node being checked, filled in blue. Blue arrows and blue rings around previously visited nodes show the search path.
result: Pointer cur compares four nodes along 8 → 4 → 6 → 7. At step four the target value 7 matches, and the search returns that node. No tree links change.

frames.title: Start at root 8
frames.explanation: Initialize cur at root 8, filled in blue. Compare target 7 with current value 8. Since 7 < 8, the target lies in the left subtree. Next move down to left child 4. Path so far: 8.
frames.key_state: Pointer cur points to root 8. Since target 7 < 8, move next to left child 4.
frames.announcement: Begin the search for 7 with cur at root 8.

frames.title: Go left to node 4
frames.explanation: Since 7 < 8, execute cur = cur.left, following the blue arrow from 8 to left child 4. Compare target 7 with current value 4: since 7 > 4, search next in the right subtree of 4. Path: 8→4.
frames.key_state: Pointer cur is at 4 (path 8→4). Since 7 > 4, the next node is right child 6.
frames.announcement: Since 7 is smaller than 8, cur moves from 8 to left child 4.

frames.title: Go right to node 6
frames.explanation: Since 7 > 4, execute cur = cur.right, following the blue arrow from 4 to right child 6. Compare target 7 with current value 6: since 7 > 6, continue to the right child of 6. Path: 8→4→6.
frames.key_state: Pointer cur is at 6 (path 8→4→6). Since 7 > 6, the next node is right child 7.
frames.announcement: Since 7 is larger than 4, cur moves from 4 to right child 6.

frames.title: Find node 7
frames.explanation: Since 7 > 6, execute cur = cur.right and follow the blue arrow from 6 to right child 7. The value at cur matches target 7, so the loop exits and returns node 7. Path: 8→4→6→7.
frames.key_state: Pointer cur points to target node 7 (path 8→4→6→7). Search successful.
frames.announcement: Since 7 is larger than 6, cur moves from 6 to right child 7 and finds the target.
